issues.description: Add a paired accept-case test for statement-form `@layer foo;` before `@import`.
issues.detail: All three reviewers note the new test only pins the reject side (`@layer foo {}` before `@import`). The complementary fact — that statement-form `@layer foo, bar;` before `@import` remains valid — is the other half of the spec invariant and should be locked down so a future tightening of the predicate cannot silently flip it. Torvalds additionally suggests a non-empty block fixture to prove the fix is not keying on emptiness.

issues.description: Extract the layer-shape check into a named predicate instead of an inline `typeof` test.
issues.detail: All three reviewers flag `!(nodeName === 'layer' && typeof node.nodes === 'undefined')` as a PostCSS-shape test masquerading as domain logic inside an already-busy boolean. A small helper like `isLayerStatementWithoutBlock(node)` (or simply `!node.nodes`) names the concept being tested, reads as data about node shapes rather than a clever condition, and survives future PostCSS node-shape changes.

issues.description: Document the CSS cascade-spec invariant the predicate encodes.
issues.detail: The clause silently encodes a real rule: statement-form `@layer name;` is allowed before `@import`, but block-form `@layer name {}` is a style rule that disqualifies later imports. A one-line comment stating that invariant above the check would save the next maintainer a spec lookup and prevent accidental tightening or loosening during refactors.

synthesis.summary: The panel unanimously accepts the fix: it correctly distinguishes statement-form `@layer name;` (allowed before `@import` per the CSS Cascade spec) from block-form `@layer name {}` (a style rule that disqualifies later imports), and the change is small, focused, and behaviorally right. All three reviewers raise the same three taste-level concerns: the inline `typeof node.nodes === 'undefined'` check should be a named predicate, the spec invariant should be stated as a comment, and the test suite should pin both sides of the invariant (the still-allowed statement-layer case, ideally plus a non-empty block fixture). No blockers; accept with trivial fixup.
